evidence.quote: Effectively, we’re saying that rates will remain highly accommodative until the economy is far along in its recovery, and that, that should be a very powerful statement in supporting economic activity.
overall, inflation is running well below our 2 percent longer-run objective.
the labor market has improved, but it’s a long, long way from maximum employment, and it will be some time getting back there.
over coming months we will continue to increase our “holdings of Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities at least at the current pace.”
if we don’t get that, then there would certainly be downside risks through the— certainly through the channel I mentioned.
And even after, if we do lift off, we will keep policy accommodative until we actually have a moderate overshoot of inflation for some time.

parsed.rationale: The Chair introduces strengthened outcome-based guidance to hold rates at zero until maximum employment and an inflation overshoot, while continuing $120 billion in monthly purchases. He stresses below-target inflation, a labor market far from maximum employment, and downside risks if fiscal support lapses.
